newsitem.title: POLAND: S.Africa 160,000 rand offshore cap seen next week.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa 160,000 rand offshore cap seen next week.

text.p: South Africa is likely to decide on its ceiling for individual investment abroad at about 160,000 rand next week, South Africa's Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Wednesday.
"The limit has not been set yet but between the finance ministry and the reserve bank we have been talking about a limit of around 160,000 Rand," Stals told a news conference in Warsaw.
"When we get back to South Africa...next week we will finalise the figure, but it is more or less the kind of figure we were thinking about," he added.
South Africa plans effectively to lift foreign exchange controls for ordinary citizens on July 1 but it has yet to announce an exact amount of the limit for offshore investments.
South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said earlier on Wednesday during a visit to Tokyo that the cap was unlikely to be set below 160,000 rand.

Stals said there should be some demand for foreign currencies as a result of the July 1 liberalisation but that the time for the move was right as capital flows into the country and foreign reserves had grown for the last six months.
"We are not afraid that the outflow of capital, because of this new concession, will have any big effect on the exchange rate or the foreign reserves," the central bank chief said.
"The Reserve Bank is very well prepared to sell foreign exchange if necessary to accommodate this outflow of capital," the governor said after meeting his Polish counterpart.
